candidate.name: Gravity-Compensating Hydraulic Damper
candidate.mechanism: Passive hydraulic damper that increases flow resistance proportionally to postural pressure changes, preventing overdrainage in upright position without electronics
candidate.causal_path: Posture change → pressure differential → damper compresses → resistance increases → flow limited
candidate.key_assumption: Hydraulic damper response time < postural pressure change rate
candidate.strongest_alternative: Anti-siphon device (ASD) — passive but fixed threshold, doesn't adapt to individual patient
candidate.killer_experiment: Bench: damper in mock CSF loop, apply postural pressure steps, measure flow regulation

attacks.verdict: Alternative: Anti-siphon device (ASD) — passive but fixed threshold, doesn't adapt to individual patient
Mechanism is distinct from existing portfolio

candidate.name: Self-Referencing Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor with Zero-Drift Compensation
candidate.mechanism: Dual-element piezoresistive sensor where one element measures pressure and the other is sealed at reference pressure, enabling real-time zero-drift compensation through differential measurement
candidate.causal_path: Temperature drift → both elements drift equally → differential cancels → drift-free measurement
candidate.key_assumption: Both sensor elements have matched temperature coefficients
candidate.strongest_alternative: Periodic recalibration (requires clinical visit) or optical pressure sensor (P-09, molecule not designed)
candidate.killer_experiment: Bench: dual-element sensor in temperature chamber, measure drift vs single-element over 30 days

candidate.name: Adaptive Drainage Rate Controller with CSF Production Estimation
candidate.mechanism: Closed-loop controller that estimates CSF production rate from drainage/ICP trends and adjusts valve setting to match production, preventing both over and under-drainage
candidate.problem_addressed: Underdrainage (12% of failures, $30K each) AND Overdrainage (15%)
candidate.causal_path: Measure drainage+ICP → estimate CSF production → adjust valve → match production → stable ICP
candidate.key_assumption: CSF production can be estimated from drainage/ICP measurements within useful timescale
candidate.strongest_alternative: Fixed programmable valve (doesn't adapt), P-01 (predicts obstruction, doesn't match production)
candidate.killer_experiment: Simulation: virtual patient cohort with varying CSF production, compare adaptive vs fixed valve ICP stability
candidate.buyer: Shunt OEM with electronic valve capability

candidate.name: Quorum-Sensing Inhibitor Coating (QSI)
candidate.mechanism: Catheter surface coated with quorum-sensing inhibitor molecules that prevent bacterial communication, blocking biofilm formation before it starts without killing bacteria (no resistance pressure)
candidate.causal_path: Bacteria attach → attempt quorum sensing → QSI blocks signal → no biofilm formation → no infection
candidate.key_assumption: QSI molecules remain active on catheter surface in CSF for >30 days
candidate.strongest_alternative: P-11 (phage — kills bacteria, resistance possible), P-20 (glycan — immune tolerance, different mechanism), antibiotic coating (resistance emerging)
candidate.killer_experiment: In vitro: QSI-coated vs uncoated catheter in S. aureus quorum-sensing assay, 7 days

attacks.verdict: Alternative: P-11 (phage — kills bacteria, resistance possible), P-20 (glycan — immune tolerance, different mechanism), antibiotic coating (resistance emerging)
Mechanism is distinct from existing portfolio

candidate.name: Thermoelectric CSF Temperature Gradient Harvester
candidate.mechanism: Thermoelectric generator exploiting the temperature differential between CSF (37°C core) and subcutaneous tissue (~35°C), generating microwatts for implantable sensing without batteries
candidate.problem_addressed: Battery depletion (5% of failures in active shunts, $45K each)
candidate.causal_path: Core CSF at 37°C → thermoelectric generator → subcutaneous at 35°C → 2°C gradient → μW power
candidate.key_assumption: 2°C temperature gradient is maintained in chronic implant and produces useful power (>1 μW)
candidate.strongest_alternative: P-15 (cardiac motion harvesting, 10 μW P50), P-16 (NIR photovoltaic, ~1050 μW), battery (finite life)
candidate.killer_experiment: Bench: thermoelectric generator in 37°C/35°C gradient, measure power output

attacks.verdict: Problem: Battery depletion (5% of failures in active shunts, $45K each)
Thermoelectric power: 0.16 nW (need >1000 nW = 1 μW). 2°C gradient insufficient.
Alternative: P-15 (cardiac motion harvesting, 10 μW P50), P-16 (NIR photovoltaic, ~1050 μW), battery (finite life)
Mechanism is distinct from existing portfolio
